items.title: Dan Morgenstern — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then John Levy, who started out as a very good bass player and then, while he was with George Shearing, became Shearing’s road manager, then decided to go into management, and started managing people like Joe Williams, Nan

ctx.x: . . . pantheon, which has, until about five years ago, only consisted of musicians. But they decided to add a category called “jazz advocate,” which is named for A. B. Spellman, who just retired about a year ago from his 30 years at NEA in the jazz program there. My predecessors were, first, Nat Hentoff, who after all is an old mentor of mine. Then it was George Wein, who we don’t need to say – everybody knows who George was. I intersected with George too. It was George who made it possible for us to bring Art…
Thank you for being present for the easiest interview I’ve ever had to conduct.
